name: car_sedan_thermal
source: Engine thermal variant (engine thermal plan T1, vault PHYS-063): car_sedan.json unchanged except that it names a cooling system (cooling_systems/sedan.json), which is what opts a vehicle in to the lumped engine/oil thermal model; the engine thermal file comes from the engine's default_thermal. Starts warm (coolant 91 C, oil 95 C = the friction maps' reference, so the engine behaves exactly like the non-thermal car until it is cooled or the start is set to "ambient"). Original source follows. Geometry (wheelbase 2.70 m, track 1.56 m, wheel radius 0.317 m) matches data/models/car_sedan/car_sedan.rig.json. Mass (1500 kg curb weight) is a plausible round-number choice for a mid-size sedan (Genta, 'Motor Vehicle Dynamics', ch. 1 cites typical passenger-car curb weights of 1200-1700 kg). Owner ruling (2026-09-25, PHYS-033 P4 I5 prep): car_sedan is a FWD mid-size sedan, so its static front/rear split was moved from a symmetric 50/50 to 60/40 (Genta ch. 1's cited 50/50-60/40 range for passenger cars, FWD sitting at the heavy-front end) - the motivation was that the 1st-gear full-throttle launch spun the front tyres for ~3.5 s because 1st-gear drive force (~7.6 kN) exceeded the front axle's grip at 50/50 static load; more front load is the physically correct part of that fix (traction control is deferred to I5). Implementation: the chassis BodyDesc (owned by each test/scenario/adapter caller, not this file) is a box symmetric about its own body origin with no separate centre-of-mass field, so the origin IS the mass centre by construction - moving the static split therefore means moving the WHEEL attachment points relative to that fixed origin (wheelbase kept at 2.70 m: front x = +1.08 m, rear x = -1.62 m, i.e. the CoM sits 1.08 m behind the front axle / 1.62 m ahead of the rear axle, giving F_front/W = 1.62/2.70 = 0.60), not moving the chassis box or adding a CoM-offset field to ps/backend (BodyDesc/BoxShape - an engine-neutral core change, avoided as out of scope for this interim data-only pass). This DOES move the wheel attachment x relative to the chassis body/visual-model origin that data/models/car_sedan/car_sedan.rig.json's susp_* pivots (also x=+-1.35) were baked against; adapters/godot/demo/scripts/vehicle_visual.gd's existing per-wheel model-to-physics alignment (previously Z/height-only, '_align_model_to_physics_wheels', already built to absorb a small art/data disagreement - see PHYS-033 G1's tractor precedent) was generalised to also absorb the X (and Y) offset the same way, so the whole visual model (body + wheel meshes together) shifts by a constant -0.27 m along chassis-local x and the wheels still sit in the model's own (fixed, unmoved) wheel arches; only the invisible Jolt collision box (used for underbody bottoming-out only, already documented as coarser than the visible mesh) is very slightly offset from the visible body as a result - deliberately accepted as the least-machinery option pending the owner's later parametric mass/CoM/inertia editor. New corner static loads (g=9.81): front axle 0.6*1500*9.81=8829.0 N total, 4414.5 N/corner (corner mass 450.0 kg); rear axle 0.4*1500*9.81=5886.0 N total, 2943.0 N/corner (corner mass 300.0 kg). Suspension spring rates are re-derived per axle so the static-equilibrium compression again sits at 1/3 of travel_max (0.18/3=0.06 m) under the NEW corner load: front spring_rate=4414.5/0.06=73575.0 N/m, rear spring_rate=2943.0/0.06=49050.0 N/m (exact, same method as the original 50/50 value 61312.5=3678.75/0.06). Damper rates target the same ~0.35 damping ratio about the new operating point (Milliken, 'Race Car Vehicle Dynamics', ch. 16), c=2*zeta*sqrt(k*m_corner): front raw c=2*0.35*sqrt(73575.0*450.0)=4027.8 N*s/m, rounded to 4000 (matching the original file's round-to-nearest-100 style, whose 50/50 raw value 3356.5 rounded to 3400); rear raw c=2*0.35*sqrt(49050.0*300.0)=2685.2 N*s/m, rounded to 2700. Rebound rates keep the original file's bump:rebound ratio (5000/3400=25/17=1.4706, never independently re-derived from a formula in the 50/50 file either) applied to the new bump rates: front 4000*25/17=5882.4 rounded to 5900, rear 2700*25/17=3970.6 rounded to 4000. Anti-roll-bar rates (front 15000, rear 10000 N/m) are UNCHANGED - they set roll-stiffness distribution from relative left/right compression, not static load, and nothing about track width or roll-stiffness need changed. Chassis inertia is not a field in this file at all (computed by the backend from the chassis BodyDesc's box shape + mass, both unchanged by this pass) so it is untouched and bit-identical. All 4 wheels reference data/tyres/passenger_car_225_45r17.json. Powertrain (PHYS-033 I3): data/engines/i4_2l_na.json -> dry clutch -> data/gearboxes/sedan_6mt.json -> open differential (final drive 4.06, a typical 2.0 L FWD value, range 3.9-4.4) -> FL/FR. This replaces the P3 placeholder's single final_drive_ratio = 10.0, which stood in for 1st gear x differential because there was no gearbox (vault PHYS-023); overall 1st is now 3.54 x 4.06 = 14.37. Clutch: kinetic capacity 300 N*m = 1.5 x engine peak torque (typical passenger-car reserve 1.3-1.8), static factor 1.15, progressive engagement vs pedal (diaphragm-spring-like). Aero: drag_area 0.68 m^2 = Cd 0.30 x A 2.27 m^2 (typical mid-size sedan). The manual_tcu driver aids (auto-clutch, auto-blip) default ON for gamepad play; see PHYS-033 I3 plan section 8. Auto-clutch post-shift close (owner test drive 2026-09-25, "a lot of wheel spin in 2nd"): sync_time_s 0.30 / max_sync_torque_nm 50 make the reclose torque-following (clutch capacity = engine torque + min(J_engine*|slip|/sync_time_s, 50 N*m), see AutoClutchDesc::sync_time_s) instead of a fixed-rate ramp to the full 300 N*m; max_sync_torque_nm 50 N*m (~25% of peak engine torque) caps what the synchronising term adds to the driven wheels on top of the engine's own torque; sync_time_s 0.30 is the time constant the engine speed converges on the input shaft with below that cap (tests/validation/test_powertrain_auto_clutch_shifts.cpp: 1->2 and 2->3 lock within 0.4-0.9 s). close_time_s 0.20 -> 0.10: the rate e_auto follows that target at, halved so the clutch picks the engine up right after dog-in instead of letting it flare further (WOT 2->3 probe: post-shift rpm peak 4926 -> 4578, max front kappa 0.085 -> 0.068). Speed-matched upshift (owner test drive 2026-09-25, "I still see the speed ticking throughout the entire shift"): auto_blip upshift_cut_release_slip_rpm 300 holds the upshift cut through the post-shift close until the engine is within 300 rpm of the new gear's input shaft, as an AMT's ECU does; the car coasts (-0.05..-0.2 m/s^2) instead of pulling at 3.5-4 m/s^2 through a flaring engine. The engine loses the gear step on its own motoring torque (data/engines/i4_2l_na.json: ~61 N*m at 5000 rpm on 0.16 kg*m^2, ~3300-3600 rpm/s), so the torque hole (shift request -> clutch carrying the full engine demand) measures 0.78 s for a WOT 1->2 at ~6000 rpm and 0.57 s for 2->3 (tests/validation/test_powertrain_auto_clutch_shifts.cpp). upshift_cut_max_hold_s 0.6 s: above the ~0.53 s a WOT 1->2 near the 6300 rpm shift point needs, short enough that a 1->2 at a wheelspin-inflated rpm (huge gear step) does not coast for a whole second. upshift_torque_ramp_s 0.10 s brings the pedal back without a torque step.
